Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project team is delivering work in another country and must comply with the standards that apply in that jurisdiction. To be confident they are following the correct requirements, where can they find information on these local standards?
o: Assumptions based on similar past projects
Informal advice from local project team members
Standards already applied in the home country
General guidance issued by professional networks
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Local authorities publish the standards that apply in their jurisdiction.

n.0: Fiction books are not a reliable source.
n.1: Preferences do not override standards.
n.3: Travel guides are not about professional standards.
n.4: Interpretation must be guided by official sources.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project professional working in the UK must ensure their project complies with the requirements of GDPR when processing personal data. Which source is best for authoritative advice on meeting these obligations?
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: ICO is the UK's regulatory authority for data protection and GDPR.

n.0: Business news is not authoritative for GDPR compliance.
n.1: Gossip is not reliable.
n.2: Blogs may not be accurate.
n.4: Forums are not official sources.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: Why is it important to follow recognised industry standards?
o: They ensure best practice and legal compliance
They replace the need for training
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Standards provide a framework for best practice and compliance.

n.1: Personal opinions remain valuable within standards.
n.2: Profit is not guaranteed by standards.
n.3: Standards support, not limit, growth.
n.4: Ongoing training is still required.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: While seeking guidance on a technical matter, a project manager receives conflicting advice from two different sources and is unsure which to rely on. What should they do to resolve the conflict responsibly?
o: Combine both pieces of advice into a single approach
Verify the advice with authoritative and up-to-date sources
Select the advice that best fits the current plan
Follow the advice given by the more senior colleague
Escalate the disagreement to the project sponsor immediately
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Always verify advice with credible, current sources.

n.0: Speed does not guarantee correctness.
n.2: Majority opinion is not always correct.
n.3: Proceeding alone may increase risk.
n.4: Cost should not be the only factor.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project is subject to newly introduced environmental regulations, and the project manager needs to remain confident that the team is always working to the current requirements. What is the most reliable way for them to stay informed?
o: Ignore updates until requested by a client
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Official updates are the best way to stay compliant.

n.0: Proactive compliance is better than reactive.
n.1: Non-specialists may not have the correct information.
n.2: Media coverage may be delayed or incomplete.
n.3: Annual reviews are not frequent enough for compliance.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: While preparing deliverables, a project professional finds they are unsure whether their work meets a particular technical standard that applies to their field. Taking a professional approach, what is the best way for them to resolve this uncertainty?
o: Apply the standard that was used on a previous, broadly similar project
Ask the project team for a majority view on the standard
Escalate to the sponsor and ask them to make the decision
Proceed and rely on quality control to catch any gaps
Consult the relevant professional body or standard-setting organisation
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: A professional seeks authoritative, specialist advice when unsure: the body that sets or maintains the standard is the right source.

n.0: A previous project may have applied a different or outdated standard; the current, relevant one must be checked.
n.1: A majority view is not authoritative; compliance is a matter of fact, not opinion.
n.2: The sponsor directs the project but is not a technical authority on the standard.
n.3: Proceeding while unsure is unprofessional; quality control may catch the gap too late or not at all.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project manager needs authoritative guidance on a demanding technical matter and wants to demonstrate good practice in how they source specialist advice. Which of the following is the best example of using a specialist source for advice?
o: Asking an experienced colleague from an unrelated discipline
Asking the sponsor to make the technical judgement
Relying on a general internet search for the answer
Following what was done on the last similar project
Contacting a chartered engineer for technical guidance
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: A chartered engineer is a professionally qualified specialist in the relevant field, so they are an authoritative source for a demanding technical matter.

n.0: Experience in an unrelated discipline does not make someone a specialist in this matter.
n.1: The sponsor is accountable for the business case but is not a technical specialist.
n.2: A general search is not a verified, authoritative specialist source.
n.3: Past practice may not fit the current matter or reflect current standards.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project team delivering a new manufacturing line wants to confirm that their approach meets the current, authoritative requirements for quality management before an external assessment. Where should they look to verify that their project satisfies the latest recognised standards?
o: Guidance issued by the Health and Safety Executive
Internal project quality reports from earlier phases
The organisation's general operational policy handbook
Benchmarking data gathered from competitor products
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Quality standards like ISO 9001 provide authoritative requirements.

n.0: Feedback is valuable but not a source of standards.
n.1: Meeting minutes record decisions, not standards.
n.2: Magazines are not an appropriate source.
n.3: Old materials may be out of date.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project manager is initiating a project in a heavily regulated sector where breaches carry significant consequences. Being aware of the relevant legal and regulatory requirements is essential for what primary reason?
o: To ensure the project operates within the law and meets required standards
To reduce the amount of project documentation needed
To transfer all legal accountability onto the project sponsor
To limit the involvement of external regulatory bodies
To justify extending the project schedule and budget
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Operating within the law is essential for project legitimacy and success.

n.1: Delegation does not remove legal obligations.
n.2: Profit is not the only concern for managers.
n.3: Communication is vital for compliance.
n.4: Meetings are still necessary for coordination.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: Midway through delivery, a project manager is notified that a new regulation affecting working conditions has come into force. Before taking any further action, what should the project manager do first?
o: Update the project plan before reviewing the regulation
Escalate the regulation to the sponsor for a decision
Implement the regulation immediately without any impact analysis
Add the regulation directly to the project risk register
Review the regulation and assess its impact on the project
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Assessment ensures the project is aligned with the new regulation.

n.0: Assumptions may be incorrect.
n.1: Managers must understand the regulation before delegating.
n.2: Ignoring regulations increases risk.
n.3: Change may be needed to comply.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project sponsor asks the project manager to consider how newly introduced health and safety regulations could affect the delivery of a construction project. Which aspect of the project are these regulations most likely to affect?
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Health and safety regulations govern how work is carried out on site, such as safe systems of work, equipment, welfare and hours, so their main effect is on working conditions.

n.0: Communication channels may carry safety messages, but the regulations mainly change how work is done.
n.1: The benefits timetable depends on when outputs are adopted, not directly on safety regulations.
n.2: Belbin team roles describe behavioural strengths and are unaffected by safety regulations.
n.3: The reimbursement method is a commercial choice about how suppliers are paid; safety law does not set it.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project manager is planning a project in a country with strict environmental laws. Which area is most likely to require extra attention?
o: Leadership style of the project manager
Choice of reimbursement method for suppliers
Format of the earned value reports
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Strict environmental law affects sustainability and compliance most directly: permits, emissions, waste, materials and reporting duties.

n.0: Leadership style is chosen to suit the team, not driven by environmental law.
n.1: Reimbursement method depends on scope certainty and risk allocation, not environmental law.
n.2: Communication frequency depends on stakeholder needs, not environmental regulation.
n.3: Report format is an internal reporting choice unaffected by environmental law.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: During a governance review, a project board is reminded that the project operates within a strict legal framework. If the project fails to comply with the relevant legislation, this failure can most likely lead to which of the following?
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Non-compliance can cause serious legal and reputational consequences.

n.1: Success is not guaranteed by non-compliance.
n.2: Customers may lose trust after non-compliance.
n.3: Funding can be withdrawn due to legal issues.
n.4: Legal breaches always have consequences.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: While reviewing their delivery plan, a project team discovers that some current activities conflict with newly introduced risk management regulations. To act responsibly and remain compliant, what should the team do?
o: Pause and update project processes to comply
Only apply changes to non-critical areas
Continue as planned and hope for the best
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Pausing and updating ensures compliance and reduces risk.

n.1: Specialist or legal advice is also needed.
n.2: Ignoring rules can result in penalties.
n.3: All areas must comply, not just non-critical.
n.4: Proceeding without compliance increases risk.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: How can the regulatory environment impact project governance?
o: By deciding the project's estimating method
By setting the team's preferred conflict resolution style
By fixing the sequence of activities on the critical path
By setting requirements for oversight and reporting
By choosing the team's leadership style
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Regulation affects governance by imposing approvals, audits, reporting duties and oversight requirements (for example data protection or health and safety duties).

n.0: The estimating method is a planning choice for the project team.
n.1: Conflict handling style is chosen to suit the situation, not set by regulation.
n.2: The critical path comes from the project's own activity dependencies, not regulation.
n.4: Leadership style is chosen by the manager to suit the team and situation.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project manager is explaining to a new team member how external legislation relates to the way risk is handled on the project. Which of the following best describes the role that legislation plays in project risk management?
o: It transfers all project risk to the regulatory body
It sets the maximum risk exposure a project may accept
It defines minimum standards for managing and mitigating risk
It replaces the project's own risk management process
It determines the contingency budget held for risk
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Laws and regulations provide baseline requirements for risk processes.

n.0: No project can be made totally risk-free.
n.1: Insurance and risk management work together.
n.3: Uncertainty is always present in projects.
n.4: Risk management is always necessary.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project's completion date has slipped because newly introduced regulations require additional safety checks to be carried out before handover. This delay is best described as an example of which of the following?
o: Scope creep introduced by additional requirements
Ineffective risk response to a known threat
Poor initial estimation of the project timeline
Legal and regulatory impact on project schedule
Resource shortfall affecting planned project activities
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: New laws can alter timelines and project plans.

n.0: Budget is not the issue here.
n.1: Stakeholder mapping is unrelated to safety checks.
n.2: Team conflict is not the cause in this scenario.
n.4: Project methodology may need adapting, but is not the cause here.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A client formally requests assurance that a project has met all applicable environmental regulations before accepting the deliverables. To satisfy this request, what should the project manager provide?
o: Documentation demonstrating adherence to legal standards
A list of team members’ qualifications
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Evidence-based documentation proves compliance.

n.0: Opinions are not evidence of compliance.
n.1: Social events are irrelevant.
n.3: Marketing is not compliance evidence.
n.4: Qualifications are unrelated to environmental standards.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: New regulations come into force requiring that every member of staff working on a project completes mandatory health and safety training. In relation to this requirement, what is the project manager's responsibility?
o: Schedule the required training after the project has closed
Ensure all team members complete the required training
Record the required training as an optional development activity
Arrange the required training only for newly recruited staff
Provide the required training solely to supervisory staff
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Managers must ensure all mandatory training is completed.

n.0: Regulatory training is not optional.
n.2: Oversight is necessary to ensure compliance.
n.3: All staff must be trained, not just management.
n.4: Delaying training risks non-compliance.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: How can changes in legislation affect project sustainability practices?
o: By eliminating the use of sustainable materials
By focusing solely on short-term outcomes
By requiring adoption of new environmental standards
By removing the need for documentation
By reducing the importance of sustainability
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: New laws may set higher standards for sustainability.

n.0: Sustainable materials may be required, not eliminated.
n.1: Long-term outcomes remain a focus.
n.3: Documentation is usually still required.
n.4: Sustainability remains important under regulation.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A contractor delivering a construction project is required to comply fully with workplace safety laws throughout the works. In terms of the project's people, what is the primary benefit of this compliance?
o: Improved working conditions for the team
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Compliance improves health, safety, and wellbeing at work.

n.1: Profit is not guaranteed by compliance.
n.2: Compliance may actually slow down some processes.
n.3: Insurance may not always be affected.
n.4: Paperwork is a side effect, not the primary benefit.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project team is planning a programme of work that will be delivered across several countries, each with its own laws and standards. To manage compliance effectively, what is an essential first step for the team?
o: Identify legal and regulatory requirements for each country
Apply the same rules to all locations
Rely only on home country standards
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Identifying requirements ensures compliance in all jurisdictions.

n.0: Proactive planning is best.
n.2: Assumptions are risky.
n.3: Rules may differ by country.
n.4: Home standards may not meet foreign requirements.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project manager is assessing which external developments could force an update to the project's risk management plan. Which of the following regulatory changes is most likely to have such an impact?
o: A revised standard for electronic document formats
An increase in the national minimum wage
A new requirement for risk assessment documentation
Updated rules on the company's financial year-end dates
A change to company car tax rules
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: A new legal requirement for risk assessment documentation directly changes how risks must be assessed and recorded, so the risk management plan must be updated.

n.0: Document format standards affect information management, not the risk management plan.
n.1: A wage increase mainly affects labour costs and the budget, not the risk management approach.
n.3: Year-end rules affect financial reporting timing, not how risks are managed.
n.4: Company car tax affects employee benefits, not the project's risk process.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project is selected for an external audit to confirm that it complies with recently introduced governance regulations. When the auditors arrive, what should the project manager provide to demonstrate compliance?
o: A verbal summary of the compliance steps taken
Clear records showing how regulatory requirements are being met
Selected evidence covering only the strongest compliance areas
A statement of intent to comply in future
The project schedule showing completed milestone dates
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Audits require documented proof of compliance.

n.0: Opinions are not evidence for auditors.
n.2: Verbal assurances are insufficient.
n.3: Marketing is not the focus of governance audits.
n.4: Lack of documentation is non-compliant.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: Partway through delivery, a regulatory change comes into force that significantly increases the reporting obligations placed on the project. What is the most likely impact of this change on the project?
o: More detailed documentation will be needed
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Reporting requirements increase documentation needs.

n.0: Communication may need to increase, not decrease.
n.1: Extra requirements may increase project duration.
n.2: Meetings may be needed to review compliance.
n.4: Roles remain important for compliance.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project manager becomes aware that new sustainability legislation is due to take effect and will apply to the current project. To manage the situation responsibly, what should the project manager do?
o: Delegate the change to the sustainability team alone
Assess the change only if stakeholders raise concerns
Record the change without adjusting current processes
Review the change and update project processes accordingly
Apply the change only once it is fully enforced
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Processes must be updated to ensure ongoing compliance.

n.0: Laws must be followed.
n.1: Assuming enforcement will not occur is risky.
n.2: Expert or regulatory advice should be sought.
n.4: Delay can lead to non-compliance.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: A project sponsor is sceptical that recent legal and regulatory changes offer any value to the project. Considering the wider outcomes for the organisation, how can such legal and regulatory changes benefit a project?
o: By reducing the scope of assurance activities required
By lowering the cost of stakeholder engagement
By driving higher standards of governance and sustainability
By shortening the overall project delivery timeline
By removing the need for a formal business case
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Regulations often improve project standards and stakeholder outcomes.

n.0: Working conditions are often improved, not ignored.
n.1: Profit is not the only driver of legal change.
n.3: Compliance is mandatory, not optional.
n.4: Documentation is often increased by regulations.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: Under schedule pressure, a project manager is tempted to proceed without addressing a known legal requirement that applies to the work. If the project manager ignores this legal requirement, what is the potential impact?
o: The regulator will issue a temporary compliance exemption
The project and organisation may face penalties and reputational damage
The organisation's insurance will cover any consequences arising
The project sponsor will personally assume the resulting liability
The affected work will simply need to be repeated
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Legal breaches have negative consequences for the project and organisation.

n.0: Ignoring legal requirements can delay the project.
n.2: Reporting may increase due to breaches, not reduce.
n.3: Stakeholder approval is unlikely with non-compliance.
n.4: Morale is likely to suffer if legal risks are ignored.

Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.q: In response to newly enacted environmental laws, a project team revises its sustainability plan so that the project continues to meet its obligations. What does this action best demonstrate?
o: Responsiveness to legal and regulatory changes
Diversity, Ethics & Professionalism.w: Updating plans to reflect new laws shows responsible project management.

n.0: Compliance is part of best practice.
n.1: Innovating while complying is possible.
n.2: Updating plans is good planning.
n.4: Stakeholder input is still important.
